full_query: Is there anti nausea medication that can be taken to allow fluids to stay down?
sentences: Yes, there are several anti-nausea medications that can help patients keep fluids down
These medications are known as antiemetics and can be particularly useful in managing nausea and vomiting
Ondansetron: Ondansetron is a serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist that is commonly used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or surgery
It is available in oral, intravenous, and dissolvable tablet forms

Metoclopramide: Metoclopramide is a dopamine antagonist that enhances gastrointestinal motility and is used to treat nausea and vomiting associated with gastroparesis, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and postoperative conditions
Prochlorperazine: Prochlorperazine is a dopamine (D2) receptor antagonist that is effective in treating severe nausea and vomiting, including that caused by migraines and chemotherapy
Promethazine: Promethazine is an antihistamine with antiemetic properties, often used to treat motion sickness, nausea, and vomiting
Dimenhydrinate: Dimenhydrinate is another antihistamine that is commonly used to prevent and treat nausea, vomiting, and dizziness caused by motion sickness
Scopolamine: Scopolamine is an anticholinergic agent that is often used in the form of a transdermal patch to prevent motion sickness and postoperative nausea and vomiting
